Commentary.Commentary: 311 can be chased down on this pitch. But should Sri Lanka lose a couple of wickets early, they could be in trouble. Stay tuned for what should be a short innings break thanks to the poor over-rate from Mathews.

It is a good pitch to bat on but the heavy breeze did not allow the Lankan bowlers to settle into any rhythm. Malinga struggled the most while the injury to Pradeep did not help the Lankans. Why Chameera did not bowl his full quota is still a mystery. He bowled decently for his 0/34 in 7 overs. Hat-trick man in the previous game, Hasaranga, got only 7 overs while Sandakan bowled his 10 in spite of going for plenty. So baffling captaincy from Mathews.

It did seem like Sri Lanka were pulling things back. The boundaries started to dry up but an impulsion towards the end will have ruined the smile on Mathews' face. One just wonders the thought behind giving Sandakan the 49th over, especially since he had not had great day till then. Pradeep was injured but what about Chameera? The 13-run over gave the visitors some much-needed momentum.

Overall, a good batting performance from Zimbabwe. They have bounced back well after their forgetful display in the previous ODI. The openers added 39 and that was followed by a mammoth 127-run stand for the second wicket. Masakadza finally broke his 50-drought with a fine century with good support from Williams and Musakanda. Then there was a bit of a stutter as the visitors added only 40 runs in the next 8 overs but lost two wickets.

Incredible finish from Zimbabwe. 30 runs came in the final 2 overs, propelling the score over 300. The pitch looks a decent one to bat on, with not much turn but still, those last 2 overs might just make a difference in the end.

SIX! A mighty hit to finish the innings! It is not a bad ball from Malinga but there is no pace on it. The ball lands on a length, around middle and a confident-looking Raza wallops down the track and sends it sailing over long on! ZIMBABWE FINISH ON 310/8!
Finally the yorker is on track, swinging in, Carl cannot do much than get an inside edge onto his boot. The ball rolls to the left of Malinga and the batsmen take a single.
A short ball outside off, Sikandar comes down the track and slaps it over cover for a single.

FOUR! FANTASTIC! That is not an easy shot to execute. Malinga holds the length back a touch and bowls it outside off, but Raza punches it through the covers. It seems like sweeper will get to it but the timing is good enough.

FOUR! It was poor from Sri Lanka on the previous ball and now it is poorer from Malinga. He dishes out a full toss and wraps the gift by bowling it on the pads. Raza is too good to miss out and clips it beautifully between square leg and mid-wicket.
Full and outside off, driven towards mid off for a quick single. Job done by Mumba but poor from Sri Lanka. They needed the new man on strike.
CURL MUMBA is the next man in, replacing Cremer!

OUT! A diamond duck for Cremer! Raza punches this short of a length ball through the off side and Cremer sets off blindly for a run, thinking that Raza should keep the strike for the final over. But what he doesn't realize is that the bowler himself is in the way. It is now a running race between the bowler and Cremer. The latter pulls out and Sandakan disturbs the stumps at his end. 13 runs from the over but 2 wickets in it for Sri Lanka. Sandakan finishes with figures of 10-0-73-1. Those do not show how well he bowled, to be honest.
GRAEME CREMER is the new man in, replacing Moor!

OUT! Straight to the man! Moor cannot make it three in a row. It is full but flatter this time, outside off and Moor mistimes his heave. It is towards long on but surprisingly it carries to Kusal Mendis who comes forward and takes a good catch. Finally, Sandakan gets a wicket in his final over. In his first 3 overs, he looked like picking up a wicket every over.

SIX! CRASH! Now this is brave hitting. Sandakan gives this one more air than the previous ball but Moor still goes after it. He chooses the slog sweep option albeit it is against the wind. However, he connects well and the ball sails over deep mid-wicket! That is real power.

SIX! Clean hitting. Sandakan is brave, tossing the ball up in the penultimate over of the innings and pays the price for it. Moor gets under it and lofts the ball with finesse over long off for a maximum.
Goes for the sweep but misses and is hit on the pads.
Full and down the leg side, swept behind square leg for a single.

FOUR! Up and over! Misses his yorker by a fraction does Malinga and that is enough for Moor. Gets under the fuller length outside off and lofts it cleanly over mid off, one bounce and into the fence. Perhaps Mathews kept himself in the ring to prevent the single.
On middle and off, clipped straight to short mid-wicket.
Full and outside off, driven back to the bowler.
An inswinging full toss on the pads, clipped through mid-wicket for one.

Another attempted yorker, but going down the leg side. Moor misses his flick and is hit on the pads. No appeal for LBW, perhaps an inside edge on that occasion. The ball rolls to point and the batsmen take a run. No signal from the umpire, so it must have been an inside edge.
Excellent inswinging yorker, tailing in late from outside off, Raza digs it out and gets a single.
Now the reverse sweep is employed, off a full toss on leg stump and it is a single to backward point.
Outside off, dabbed straight to backward point.
This time he gets it through the leg side for a single.
WIDE. Down the leg side, flick shot missed.
FOUR! That is a great shot! Outside off, a tad shorter, Moor comes forward and drives it through the covers, into the wind. Two fielders give it a chase but it is a desperate one and the balls wins.
Short and outside off, punched through the covers for a couple.
Landed around off, turning in, Raza works it with the spin through mid-wicket. Both, the keeper and the bowler go after the ball and get to it. Just a single.
PETER MOOR walks in next, replacing Waller.

OUT! PLUMB LBW! Cannot miss full tosses. If you miss, you need to pay the price. And Waller does. He bowls an inswinger, goes for the yorker but misses it. It turns out into a full toss but luckily for the bowler, Waller misses his flick as well. Is hit on the pads and umpire Ian Gould raises his finger in a flash. Boy, that looked dead and replays confirm the same. Sri Lanka strengthening their hold in the death.
A bit of a half volley now, driven through the covers for a single.
Full and in line of the stumps, watchfully defended.

WIDE. Misses the direction again. Is he struggling to control the swing? Perhaps, with the heavy breeze. Goes for the inwinging yorker, but the line is outside leg and the length is a tad fuller. Raza misses his flick.
Pushes this through mid on for one.
Another delivery down the leg side, worked away for a run.
A full toss down the leg side, Raza tickles it down to fine leg for a couple.
LASITH MALINGA is back into the attack!
The batsman works it down the leg side. One run added to the total.
Floats it wide outside off, Raza looks to defend it by coming forward but misses as the keeper takes the bails off.
SIKANDAR RAZA is the new man in, replacing Williams!

OUT! Bowled 'em! Sean Williams is gutted with himself! He was the key man for his side but has been sent back. Gunaratne serves a loopy ball around middle and leg, it skids off the deck, Williams walks far to across the off stump and exposes all his stumps. He misses it completely and the ball goes on to rattle the timber. A timely wicket for the hosts again.
Waller stays back and paddles it down to fine leg for a single.
Sean steps out and jams out a yorker towards long on for a single.
Comes from around the wicket and bowls it outside off, Waller looks to sweep but gets an inside edge on the pads as the ball rolls further away. A single taken.
Good stop! Fuller ball on middle, Sean Williams lofts it over the bowler's head. The long off fielder puts in a desperate dive and does well to stop two for his side.
Hasaranga sees Williams coming down the track and hence pulls his length back. Sean still manages it heave it down to long on for a couple.
Drops it a bit short outside off, punched past covers for a single.
Comes down track, converts it into full and flicks it through the leg side for a single.
FOUR! Gets a boundary this time! Floats it up outside off, Sean Williams comes down the track and lofts it over mid off and picks up a boundary.

Ouch that must have hurt! Tossed up delivery outside off, Williams comes down the track and smashes it straight to his partner at the other end. Waller gets a beating and looks to be in some pain. It's a dot ball.
Comes down the track and hits it down to long off for a single.
Tossed up outside off, Waller sweeps it towards fine leg for a single.
The batsman has driven it through mid-on. One run added to the total.
Another loud shout for LBW! Loopy ball outside off, Sean once again looks to sweep but misses and is hit on the back pad. They appeal but the umpire once again is not interested.
Outside off, Sean reverse sweeps it through covers for a couple.
A shout for an LBW! Tossed up on the stumps, Williams looks to sweep but misses and is hit on the pads. Maybe, it was going down leg.
Goes back and punches it towards the cover region.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Very full and wide outside off, dragged off the inner half towards long on for a single.
Waller drives it towards covers for a single.
Once again opts for the reverse sweep and this time he gets some wood on it. The ball goes towards short third man for a single.
On middle and leg, SW looks to play the revere sweep but misses and is hit on the pads.
Flatter one outside off, MW looks to steer it towards third man but gets beaten.
Tossed up around off, Sean looks to flick but gets a safe leading edge towards covers for a single.
Drags his length back, Waller pulls it to deep backward square leg for one.
Goes deep in the crease and cuts it away towards point for a single.
Outside off, a bit short, punched towards the off side for a single.
Fuller ball around off, eased through mid on for a single.
Powerplay 3 signaled! Maximum of 5 fielders are now allowed outside the 30-yard circle.
Fuller around middle, defended by lunging forward.
Short outside off, cut towards sweeper cover for a single.
Wrong 'un around off, Waller presses forward to push it towards cover. He calls for the single and gets it in the end.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads.

Wide! Around middle and turning further down the leg side, Waller misses his tuck and Dickwella collects it by moving to his left. He appeals for a caught behind but no interest shown by umpire Ian Gould.
This one turns in from around middle, Waller defends it down on the track.
Fuller ball outside off, driven towards long off for a single.
FOUR! Ends the over on a high! Very full outside off, Malcolm Waller drives it a bit square on the off side. Beats the man at backward point and finds the fence. Much-needed one the African side.
Takes a stride forward and eases it through the cover region for a single.
Loopy ball on the pads, wristed straight to short mid-wicket.
Quicker delivery outside off, defended from within the crease.
Flicked through mid-wicket for one.
On middle and leg, tucked behind square on the leg side for a single.
ASELA GUNARANTE is back on!
Too full on the pads, Sean clipped through backward square leg for a single.
Gets behind the line and defends it down.
Leading edge! A leg break around middle, turning in, Williams looks to work it away on the leg side but gets a leading edge towards mid on.
Prods forward and drives it through covers for a single.
Whipped away towards mid-wicket and a single is taken.
Stays back and defends it back down the track.
LAKSHAN SANDAKAN is back into the attack!
Goes back and wrists it through mid-wicket to keep strike.
Takes a good stride forward and drives it past covers for a single.
On middle and leg, worked away through the on side for a single.
Prods forward to a full ball and defends it down.
Tosses it up outside off, driven through covers for a single.
Around middle and leg, turned through mid-wicket for a single.
Flattish outside off, punched towards the right of the bowler who dives to stop it.
On middle and leg, Waller tucks it towards the leg side.
Flatter one outside off, chopped away on the off side for a single.
FOUR! Drops it short on middle, Sean Williams has ample of time to give the treatment. He camps back and pulls it powerfully over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Full outside off, driven once again in the same region.
Drives a full delivery towards cover.
Beaten! A googly which Waller doesn't pick at all. Comes forward to drive but the ball sneaks through and just about misses the off stump.
MALCOLM WALLER is the new man in, replacing Ervine!

OUT! Three reds and the decision stands! Tossed up delivery around middle and leg, Craig Ervine gets down on one knee to sweep but misses and is hit on the pads. A loud appeal for LBW and umpire after taking his time raises his dreaded finger. Ervine has a word with his partner and then opts for the review. Replays show it was pitched in line and would have gone on to hit the leg pole. Second wicket for Hasaranga and Sri Lanka pulling things back now.
Craig Ervine is given out LBW but he has opted for the review. Where is it pitching is the question.
Comes forward and drives it straight to mid off.
Driven down to long on for one.
Full ball outside off, reverse swept once again through backward point for a couple.
Outside off, reverse swept past short third man for a couple.
2 Wides! Down the leg side, CE misses the sweep and so does the keeper.
Loopy ball around middle, it turns away after pitching, Sean looks to defend but misses as the ball just about kisses the off pole.
Sloppy! Loopy delivery around off, Williams drives it towards covers where the fielder fumbles and concedes a couple.
Short of a length ball on off, Craig chops it towards short extra cover for one.
Flat and short on off, punched off the back foot through covers for a single.
Full on off, driven through mid off for one.
Outside off, punched towards sweeper cover for a single.

What happened there? Pradeep was about to deliver but seemed to have pulled his hamstring and is seen limping off the field. These are worry signs for the hosts as he is a good death bowler. Hope he recovers soon. Here comes ASELA GUNARATNE replacing him.
Ervine comes forward to work it away but misses and is hit on the pads. A stifled appeal for an LBW which is turned down. Maybe, pitching outside leg.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery. They pick up a single.
Tossed up outside off, bunted back to the bowler who fumbles but does well to deny the batsmen a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full around middle, driven down to long on for a single.
SEAN WILLIAMS walks out next, replacing Masakadza!

OUT! The change in bowling works! And it has fetched the big fish. Masakadza is gone. Floated outside off, it is a leg spinner and Masakadza mistimes his attempted slog sweep. Gets a top edge which seems to go into vacant area but Nuwan Pradeep runs a fair distance to his right from deep mid-wicket and takes a great catch. Masakadza departs after a wonderful knock. But one just felt that he could have waited for a bit more.
WANIDU HASARANGA is called back into the attack!
Punches it through point for a couple.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Outside off, pushed towards mid off for a quick single.
Short and outside off, cut through point for a couple.
WIDE. Overdoes the short ball and it is too high. Wided by the umpire.
Action replay of the previous delivery.
Full and straight, watchfully defended.
NUWAN PRADEEP is back into the attack!

Drinks are on the field! Sri Lanka have managed to break the threatening 127-run stand and since then it has turned out to be a good passage of play for them. Hamilton Masakadza is still out there on 108 and has Craig Ervine for company. The platform is laid for the middle order to fire but can they? Let's wait and find out...
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Another long hop, tucked through mid-wicket for a single.
Short again, outside off, cut through point for a run.
On the pads now, a tad shorter, worked through mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! This is well outside leg but Masakadza picks it on the full and reverse sweeps it past short third man for a boundary!
Full and straight, watchfully defended.
Shout for an LBW! Hurls it on a length around leg, Ervine misses the flick and is hit on the pads. They appeal but it was pitched outside leg.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground. They pick up a single.
Fuller on off, eased past covers for a single.
Good length delivery outside off, a punchy drive through covers for a couple.
Slants it away outside off, Ervine looks throws his bat but is beaten. We have seen him getting beaten on a number of times in the previous over.
Fuller in length and outside off, Ervine comes forward and pushes it towards mid off.
Bowls a yorker on middle, Hamilton jams it out.
Flatter around middle, Ervine punches it down to long on for a single.
Floated delivery around off, pushed straight to mid off.
Loopy ball on off, very full, hit down to long off for another single.
Flatter through the air outside off, punched down to long on for  a single.
FOUR! Good shot! Loopy delivery outside off, Craig Ervine leans into it and caresses it through extra cover for a boundary. That should give him some confidence.
HM plays it with an angled bat and guides it to third man. Just a single from the over.
Good length delivery outside off, Ervine punches it towards mid off and gets off the mark.
Fullish outside off, Craig opens the bat face and pushes it towards short extra cover.
Fuller in length and angling away, Ervine with no foot movement goes after it but gets beaten.
Pitches it up outside off, pushed off the front foot towards cover.
Slants it away on a length outside off, Ervine fails to get any bat on it.
DUSHMANTHA CHAMEERA comes back into the attack!
A WICKET MAIDEN FROM GUNARATNE! Tossed up ball around off, defended off the front foot. A successful over for the Lankans as they get the much-needed breakthrough.
Fuller on off, pushed straight to cover.
He has the ability to stabilize the innings and with the platform that he has got now, Zimbabweans would be pinning their hopes on him to deliver yet again.
CRAIG ERVINE walks in at number 4, replacing Musakanda.

OUT! In the air... gone! Asela Gunaratne provides the breakthrough and the 127-run stand comes to an end! Loopy ball around middle, Tarisai Musakanda heaves across the line towards wide long on. Didn't time it well and Upul Tharanga after fumbling twice does well to hold onto that one. He's disappointed at himself as he misses out on his fifty by just two runs.
Makes room but the bowler follows him, Tarisai could just punch it towards cover.
Musakanda drives the ball straight down the ground.
Fuller in length around off, defended off the front foot.
ASELA GUNARATNE is back on!
5th ODI ton for Hamilton Masakadza! And the third fastest for Zimbabwe!

A TON FOR HAMILTON! Well played! He took his time to settle down but once he got in, he just went with the flow. Raises the bat and acknowledges the cheer. Gets a warming hug from his partner and the Zimbabwe dressing room is all smiles. Can he carry on? A low full toss on the pads, clipped fine down the leg side for a brace.
Leg bye! Dishes out another yorker on leg, TM misses his flick and once again the ball rolls off the pads towards the leg side. A leg bye taken.
Malinga serves another full toss on middle, Tarisai heaves it down to long on. The fielder in the deep does well to keep them down to a couple.
Very full on middle, Musakanda misses as the ball goes off the pads towards mid-wicket.
Stays behind the line and taps it in front of the point fielder for a brisk single.
Fuller on middle, HM digs it out towards mid off. Wanted a single but is sent back.
Wide! A full toss down the wrong line. Masakadaza misses his flick and the ball goes on the bounce to Dickwella.
Good stop! Fuller around off, bunted back towards the left of the bowler who does well to stop it with a dive to deny the single.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot. One run added to the total.

FOUR! Played it really well! Not often you see a batsman in the 90s playing this kind of a shot! Floated outside off, Hamilton gets into the position and reverse sweeps it through backward point for a boundary.
Goes back and punches it towards cover.

Leg bye! Flatter through the air around leg, Tarisai looks to work it across the line but it goes off the pads towards point. The bowler is busy appealing for an LBW but the batsmen sneak in a leg bye. The throw is at the striker's end which is the wrong end. Had it been at the other one, things would have been really interesting.
Loopy ball around middle, defended off the front foot.
Fuller in length and outside off, Musakanda drives it past mid off. Mathews gives it a chase and does well to pull the ball back but in the process his slips near the boundary line. Three runs taken.

NOT OUT! Sri Lanka waste a review! Malinga comes running in and fires in a perfect toe-crusher on middle and leg, Tarisai Musakanda fails to dig it out and is hit on the shoe. A loud appeal but umpire Ian Gould shakes his head. He indicates bat and immediately Malinga has a word with Mathews for the review. He is sure that it was boot first and replays confirm the same. On checking further, we come to know that the ball was pitched in line but would have clipped the leg stump. Hence the decision stands!
Is it bat first or pad? Sri Lanka have taken a review against Tarisai Musakanda.
A low full toss on middle, TM helps it to deep backward square leg for two. 150 up for Zimbabwe and it has taken them just 34 balls to reach the third fifty.
Pierces the gap to perfection! Gets a full ball and works it right in between short mid-wicket and silly mid on for a single.
Once again serves it on a fuller length outside off, pushed through covers for a single.
Fuller in length on middle, worked nicely through short mid-wicket for a single.
A bit short outside off, TM cuts it to deep point for a couple of runs.  13 runs off the over.
Wrong 'un around middle and off, Tarisai pushes it off the back foot towards point.
Eases it down towards long off for a single.
100-run stand between Musakanda and Masakadza!

SIX! Handsome looking shot! Tossed up outside off, Masakadza dances down the track and lofts it neatly over mid off. The ball dashes straight on the ropes. The umpire confirms before signalling it as a biggie. The tone has been set by these two.
Fuller on the stumps, worked through mid-wicket for a single.

Good running but why is there no slip? Floats it up outside off, Masakadza looks to play the reverse sweep but it goes off the gloves past the keeper towards third man. Musakanda wanted the third one and forces his partner to do so. Gets it in the end.
LAKSHAN SANDAKAN is back on!

FOUR! Easy pickings those! A low full toss strayed on the pads, Musakanda helps it fine down the leg side for a boundary to end the over. We saw Zimbabwe missing out a few early on in the innings but this time they get it.
Gets across a touch and wrists it straight to the silly mid on fielder.
Touch fuller outside off, Tarisai drives it through covers for a couple of runs.
Yorker on the off stump, HM does well to dig it out towards covers for a single.

Almost carries towards the fielder! A low full toss around middle, Hamilton bunts it uppishly towards the man at silly mid on. Luckily, the ball goes on the bounce to the man who was brought in on the previous ball.
Silly mid on in place...
Fuller in length on middle, Masakadza pushes it down to long on. He saw the fielder in the deep not charging towards the ball and hence calls for two. Gets it comfortably in the end.
LASITH MALINGA is called back into the attack! Can he get a breakthrough here?
Fuller on middle and off, pushed off the front foot towards mid off.

SIX! That's gone the distance! Gunaratne keeps it full, it's in the slot for Musakanda. He swings hard across the line and gets enough connection behind the shot as the ball sails over the long on fence for a biggie.
Slower through the air around middle, tucked off the pads towards square leg for nothing.
Fuller on off, milked down to long off for a single.
Loopy delivery around off, Masakadza defends it off the front foot.
Good length delivery outside off, Hamilton goes back and punches it straight towards short extra cover.
Third full toss of the over, reverse swept past Lasith Malinga at short third man for a couple.
Full and outside off, pushed towards cover.
Full and outside off, pushed towards mid off for a quick single. A direct hit at the bowler's end is missed but guess Masakadza was in.
A yorker, not a bad ball and Hamilton is forced to defend.
FOUR! Another full toss. Comes down the track and blasts it over mid on for consecutive boundaries!
FOUR! Nicely done. A full toss outside leg, Masakadza reverse sweeps it behind point for a boundary!
Full and around leg, swept through mid-wicket for a single.

FOUR! Not a bad ball though. It is in line of the stumps and Masakadza looks to go straight back over the bowler's head. Gets the execution just about right because the ball hits the toe end of the bat and goes in the direction he wants.
Around off, watchfully blocked.

A seam-up delivery, pitched on off, Masakadza looks to sweep but misses and is hit on the pads. Niroshan Dickwella appeals for an LBW, the only person to do so but no one else is interested. Mathews indicates that it was going past the off stump.
On middle and leg, blocked towards short mid-wicket.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
ASELA GUNARATNE to bowl now. Spin or medium pace? The latter for now.
The batsman got into position early and reverse swept that one. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. One run added to the total.
Full and down the leg side, Tarisai goes for the sweep but misses and is hit on the pads.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
FOUR! Welcome! The hat-trick man is a short to start today, the googly again and Musakanda pulls him over mid-wicket for a boundary!
WANIDU HASARANGA into the attack!
Another googly, Masakadza looks to work it through the leg side but is completely beaten.
FOUR! CRASH! Tossed  up outside off, Masakadza gets underneath it and smashes the ball straight back over the bowler for a boundary!
Full and down the leg side, swept fine for a single.
Much fuller and Tarisai comes forward to defend.
Change of angle now. Sandakan switches to around the wicket. He is cutting the crease in front of the umpire.

FOUR! That is short from Sandakan, something which has been an issue with him today. The length. Musakanda is more than happy to play that, even though it is a wrong 'un, which he has struggled to pick. Goes back and punches it through the covers for a boundary. 50-RUN STAND IS UP! Good buildup after the decent opening stand.
Full and down the leg side, Musakanda looks to paddle it fine but the ball hits the back of the bat and almost lobs back to the bowler.

Drinks are on the field! Zimbabwe are going great guns at the moment but they aren't reading Sandakan at all. If they manage to see off him and then go hard at others, they can very well feel they can get a big score here...
The batsman drives this through the covers. One run added to the total.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers for a single.
FOUR! Do not bowl short to these blokes. Masakadza loves it. Gets back in a flash and pulls it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Outside off, punched off the back foot.
The batsman has played it to the point region. One run added to the total.
Banged in short, pulled to deep mid-wicket for a single.
The batsman has swept that one through the leg side for one.
Full on middle, pushed down to long on for a run.
31st ODI fifty for Hamilton Masakadaza!

Half century for Masakadza! It has come after 10 innings in ODIs and if you look at the time span, it has been more than 18 months! His last 50-plus was way back in January 2016, against Afghanistan in Sharjah where he made a brilliant 110. Coming to the ball, it is swept fine for a single.
Comes forward and blocks this one out.
Full and down the leg side, swept away for a couple.
Full and on middle, pushed down to long on for a single.
FOUR! Fine shot. A short ball outside off, Masakadza goes back and cuts it behind point for a boundary!
The batsman was beaten and missed the line of the delivery.
A short ball outside off, Muskanda quickly gets onto that and pulls it through mid-wicket for a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
A short ball now, pulled wide of mid-wicket for a single.
Full and outside off, driven onto the ground over the bowler who parries it to mid off.
A short ball down the leg side, Musakanda rocks back to pull but misses and is hit on the pads. seems like a wicket is around the corner to Sandakan.
On middle, pushed back to the bowler.
WIDE. A moral victory for the bowler. It is wide outside off, but the googly again. TM does not pick it again and tries to cut it after the ball bounces, clearly being late. Misses.

There is the wrong 'un and ALMOST gets a wicket. Tarisai does not pick it at all, trying to work it to the leg side from well outside off and gets a leading edge which nearly carries back to the bowler.
A bit short now, pulled away but straight to short mid-wicket again.
The leg break now, around middle and off, Musakanda plays it off the back foot towards short mid-wicket.
Full and around off, pushed defensively off the front foot to the off side.
Full and wide outside off, driven through point for a couple.
Down the leg side, tickled into the empty space at long leg. Should have been a couple because the fielder had a long way to get to the ball but the batsmen are happy with the single. Poor running.
A short ball again, awkwardly fended once more by the batsman.

OUCH! What happened? Not quite sure whether Musakanda picked it. The ball was short from Chameera but Musakanda was late in playing at it. He tried to work it pretty late and missed it totally, getting hit on the shoulder.
Full and outside off, pushed towards mid off.
Full and wide outside off, crunched through point for a single. Moves to 40 from 39 balls.

The wrong 'un, not picked, pulled wide of long on where Lasith Malinga ambles to the ball so slowly that the batsmen do not even have to run. A simple jog will enable the second. The stand is worth 21 from 21 balls now. 9 from the first Sandakan over but there were some questions posed by the bowler.
Pushes this through mid on for one more.
Now this is short and is cut hard but there is insurance in the deep at sweeper cover. Just a run.
Landed around off, watchfully defended.
FOUR! CRACK! Picked up the length in a trice. Not an easy shot to play. It is not that short but Musakanda rocks on to his back foot quickly and pulls it through mid-wicket for a boundary!
Fullish on middle, pushed down to long on for a single.
Time for spin straightaway. LAKSHAN SANDAKAN into the attack now.
Powerplay 2 signaled. Maximum of 4 fielders are now allowed outside the 30-yard circle.
Gets behind the line and defends it down gently.
Outside off, Masakadza looks to cut but his bottom hand comes off but still is able to beat the man at point for a single.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
FOUR! Fuller length on middle and off, Hamilton comes forward and lofts it over mid on for a boundary.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Angles in a full length delivery on middle, the batsman looks to flick but gets a leading edge towards point.
Outside off, Hamilton dabs it towards point. The fielder dives all over it and that allows them to take the single.
Did you know? Today is Zimbabwe's bowling coach, MAKHAYA NTINI's birthday. He turns 40. The team can give him a nice birthday present with a win. Possible?
Hamilton pushes this full length delivery on the up towards mid on.
Good length delivery outside off, punched off the back foot towards the off side.
Good length delivery on middle and leg, Hamilton flicks it through mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
In the channel outside off, it's left alone.
FOUR! Cracking shot! Gets a full length delivery outside off, Masakadaza leans into it and cracks it through covers. That was hit brilliantly and got the desired result.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat. A successful over from Pradeep.
Fuller and angling in, Tarisai looks to defend but misses ans is hit on the pads.
Good length outside off, Musakadza looks to defend but gets an inside edge on the pads.
TARISAI MUSAKANDA is the new man in, replacing Mire.

OUT! Solomon is gone! This is lovely bowling! Pradeep sticks to the plan. He goes wide of the crease and bowls a pin point yorker on middle, Mire comes forward to counter it but is undone by the pace on it. Gets rapped on the pads and umpire Ian Gould has no hesitation in ruling it out. Solomon walks towards his partner to ask for the review but Hamilton doesn't show any interest. Replays show it was in line and would have hit the middle stick.

How did that miss the off stump? Fuller in length and comes in from wide outside off, it doesn't rise as Mire tries to hit it across the line. Is undone by the lack of bounce and the ball nearly kisses the off stump and rolls towards the keeper.
Good length delivery on middle, pushed towards mid on.
FOUR! Boom! Fuller in length and outside off, Masakadza drives it hard. It ball thuds into the turf and goes on the bounce over the man at extra cover for a boundary.
Once again angles it on on middle, Masakadza misses his flick as the ball goes off the pads towards point.
On a length and coming in from outside off, Hamilton looks to cut but fails to get any bat on it.
Fuller and angling in, Masakadza misses his flick shot and wears it on the back pad. Once again going down leg.
Good length delivery on middle, Hamilton punches it down the ground but Malinga from mid on is quick to stop that one.
Back of a length outside off, Masakadza looks to poke at it but the ball bounces a bit more and just whizzes past the outside edge to the keeper.
First bowling change as DUSHMANTHA CHAMEERA comes into the attack!
Good length delivery outside off, defended off the back foot.
This one comes back in sharply from outside off, Mire looks to hit it hard but fails to get any wood on it.

FOUR! Fuller in length and around off, Mire swings his bat across the line but gets it off the inner half. It beats the dive of the fielder at short mid-wicket and then goes past the mid on fielder for a boundary. Not convincing that, but Mire will take it.
Fullish outside off, driven uppishly towards mid off.

A huge shout for an LBW! Once again Pradeep goes wide of the crease and angles it in on middle, Mire looks to work it across the line but misses and is hit on the pads. A loud appeal to which the umpire doesn't respond. Pradeep asks Mathews regarding the referral but the skipper shows no interest. Replays show the ball would have gone on to clip the top of middle stump.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Fuller in length on off, clipped towards mid on by shuffling across. It went on the bounce to the fielder there.

Malinga hits the deck hard but it's comfortably down the leg side. Masakadza moves inside the line to let it be. The umpire for some reason doesn't call it a wide and signals it's second one of the over.
FOUR! Second one of the over! Zimbabwe are scoring boundaries at will now! Shortish in length, angling down leg, Masakadza just helps it through square leg for another boundary.
Bangs in a short ball on middle, HM ducks to let it sail over him to the keeper.
Length delivery outside off, defended with the full face of the bat.
FOUR! Classical! Two-in-two for Zimbabwe! Fuller in length and just outside off, enough room for Hamilton to free his arms. He just flays it through covers. Not a soul moves there.

FOUR! Pulled away! Short of a length delivery on middle, it comes up at a good height too. Mire stands tall and pulls it over mid-wicket. The ball bounces just before the rope. It almost traveled the distance. A nice way to end the over.
Fullish on off, Mire drives it straight to the fielder at mid off.
Length delivery on middle and leg, wristed towards the leg sdie.

A shout for an LBW! Pradeep goes wide of the crease and angles in a full length delivery on middle and leg, Solomon Mire looks to flick it across the line but misses and is rapped on the pads. A loud appeal for an LBW by Pradeep but umpire Ian Gould shakes his head. Seemed like it's going down leg.
On a length and outside off, HM looks to tap and run but gets an inside edge as the ball rolls off the pads towards first slip. Another brisk single taken.
Good length delivery on middle and leg, Hamilton tucks it towards mid-wicket.
Down the leg side, flicked behind square on the leg side for a single to end the over.
Fuller on off, kept out off the front foot.

FOUR! Nicely done, Hamilton! Just fuller around middle, Masakadza just eases it down the ground past the non-striker. The mid on fielder is placed a bit wide which means he had no chance to stop that one.
Masakadza has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Just a single off the Free Hit! Good ball. Malinga delivers a yorker at the base of the middle stump, Mire could just dig it out towards widish mid on. One run added to the total.
Free Hit time! Can Zimbabwe make the most of it?
Malinga Oversteps! Bowls a fuller ball on middle, Masakadza pushes it towards mid on. The fielder dives to stop it but they still pick the single.
Fuller in length on off, HM presses forward and defends it with his bat close to the pads.
Marginally ahead of a length around off, SM defends it down gently.
Stays put and keeps it out with a straight bat.

Shortish in length, in the corridor outside off, Hamilton dabs it towards backward point and calls for a single. The fielder charges towards the ball and has an underarm shy at the striker's end. It hits but Solomon was easily in.

FOUR! That's a good looking shot! Hurls it on a back of a length, just outside off, Masakadza punches it through the line. Gets it off the middle of the bat and away she races for a boundary through covers. First boundary of the day for Zimbabwe.
Good length delivery on off, defended solidly off the front foot.

Back of a length on middle, Mire goes back and pulls it through mid-wicket. It's through the gap but the outfield isn't that quick and that allows Gunathilaka to pull the ball back with ease. They run three.
NUWAN PRADEEP to bowl with the second new ball. Two slips for him as well.
Slower one around middle and leg, clipped towards mid on for a single.
Keeps it nice and full on middle and off, SM shuffles a touch and bunts it back towards Malinga.
Good length delivery on off, Solomon stays behind the line and keeps it out.
On a fuller length and a tinge of swing there, Mire prods forward and defends it towards cover.

Strays on the pads, Hamilton just clips it through square leg to get off the mark. There wasn't a fine leg in place so just a tickle fine would have fetched him a boundary but in this case he will have to settle for a single.
Starts off with a length delivery outside off, Masakadza shoulders his arms to that one.

It's time to get underway. The players and umpires have made their way out to the middle. The two Zimbabwe openers are - HAMILTON MASAKADZA and SOLOMON MIRE. Sri Lanka to begin with LASITH MALINGA first up. A couple of slips in place for him. Here we go!!!

TEAM NEWS - Sri Lanka are unchanged from the last game. Zimbabwe have made 2 changes - TARISAI MUSAKANDA and CARL MUMBA replace Donald Tiripano and Ryan Burl. Angelo Mathews says that there is a hint of grass on the wicket but it should not change much. Hence the decision to chase. Agrees that wind will be a key factor and a big challenge. Wants his bowlers to adjust their lines and lengths quickly. Feels that it is a must-win game for both teams for momentum. Cremer says that he would have batted first anyways. Observes that some of the plates on the wicket have started to move already, so come the afternoon, he expects a lot of turn. Like Mathews, he too, admits that the conditions are tough and will challenge both batsmen and bowlers. On the previous game, he feels that one area where they could improve is to hit the ball down the ground instead of in the air. Stresses that his side is still confident and expects his batsmen to adapt soon.

PITCH REPORT - Russel Arnold and Ed Rainsford doing the pitch report say it's really windy out there. Add that for the batsman it's hitting with the wind. Further say there are a lot of factors that they are unsure of. Inform it's a bit dry and history suggests that there are a lot of runs on it. Continue to say you need to show some application if you are to score big and the captain who LOSES the toss should do what they he is being told to do.
TOSS - SRI LANKA WIN THE TOSS AND OPT TO BOWL!

Hello and a warm welcome for the third ODI between Sri Lanka and Zimbabwe at Hambantota. After creating history in the opening encounter, the African side were brought down to earth as they were completely outclassed in the next one. Sri Lanka turned things around remarkably to square the series 1-1 and the hosts would look to continue in the same vein and carry the momentum forward. The question arises is how the strip here would turn out to be. Can the Lankans take a lead or will Zimbabwe bounce back? Stay tuned as the toss isn't far away.
